problem.title: Frankl union-closed sets conjecture under frozen empty-set and ground-set conventions
problem.informal_statement: Resolve Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture: every finite union-closed family F with at least one nonempty member contains an element of its ground set belonging to at least half the members of F. Union closure is frozen as closure under the union of any two members, including a member with itself. The empty set is permitted as a member and is counted in card(F). Element ranges over U(F), the union of all members. The half condition is the integer comparison 2 * frequency >= card(F). Both a proof and an exact finite counterexample are acceptable outcomes. A theorem for a bounded structural class is progress toward the conjecture and never its resolution; the bounded first slice attacks one such class, the union-closures of linear 3-uniform generating systems, as a waypoint that restricts the target in no way. Novelty and significance are not_assessed, and rediscovery risk is higher for the full conjecture than for any subclass because the literature is extensive.

target_claim.statement: For every finite family F of finite sets such that A union B is in F for all A, B in F (including the case A = B), and such that F has at least one nonempty member, let U(F) be the union of all members of F. Then there exists x in U(F) such that 2 * card({A in F : x in A}) >= card(F), where card(F) is the number of distinct members of F and counts the empty set when the empty set is a member.

assumption_claims.statement: A finite family F of finite sets is union-closed iff for every A in F and every B in F, including the case A = B, the union A union B is a member of F. The empty set is permitted as a member of F. Closure is required for the union of any two members, which for finite F is equivalent to closure under the union of any nonempty subfamily.

The hypothesis that F has at least one nonempty member is an explicit hypothesis of the frozen target and is not derived from anything else. It excludes exactly two degenerate families: the empty family F = {} and the family F = {empty set}, for both of which U(F) is empty and no element exists to be exhibited. Every other union-closed family is in scope.

The ground set is U(F), the union of all members of F. The word element ranges over U(F) and over nothing else; in particular it does not range over members of F, and it does not range over an ambient set chosen independently of F. The frequency of x is freq_F(x) = card({A in F : x in A}), an exact nonnegative integer.

card(F) is the number of distinct members of F. When the empty set is a member it is counted, so the empty set contributes to card(F) while contributing to no frequency. This is the harder of the two counting conventions and it is frozen; the convention that excludes the empty set from card(F) is a different statement and is not claimed.

The bounded first slice attacks one structural class as a waypoint, and the class restricts the frozen target in no way. A linear 3-uniform generating system is a family G = {A_1, ..., A_m} with m >= 1 of pairwise distinct sets, each of cardinality exactly 3, with card(A_i intersect A_j) <= 1 for all i != j. Its union-closure is F(G) = { union of A_i over i in S : S subset of {1,...,m} }, where the empty index set yields the empty set. Every F(G) is a union-closed family with at least one nonempty member, so it is an instance of the frozen target and never a weakening of it.

For any finite family G, the set of all unions of subfamilies of G is union-closed and contains the empty set, because the union of the union over S and the union over T is the union over S union T. Every finite union-closed family containing the empty set arises this way from some G, for instance from the family of its own members.

A theorem establishing the half-frequency conclusion for any bounded structural class, including the waypoint class of the first slice, is progress toward the frozen target and is never its resolution. It must be reported as a class theorem with the class stated exactly, and no report, summary, or status line may present it as the conjecture being settled. The same holds for exhaustion of any finite enumeration envelope.

When the m generators of a linear 3-uniform generating system are pairwise disjoint, the 2^m subfamily unions are pairwise distinct, so card(F) = 2^m, and every x in U(F) lies in exactly the unions indexed by sets containing the single generator that contains x, giving freq_F(x) = 2^(m-1) = card(F)/2 for every x. The frozen inequality is therefore attained with equality for arbitrarily large families, so it cannot be strengthened to a strict inequality, and the waypoint class is tight rather than slack, which is why it is worth attacking.

When generators overlap, distinct index sets can have equal unions, so card(F) < 2^m in general. card(F) must be computed from the deduplicated canonical member set and never from the number of generators or from 2^m. The same warning applies to any generator-based encoding of a general union-closed family.

The planning dossier reports that Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture has extensive literature and a deceptively simple statement, creating high rediscovery and hidden-hypothesis risk. This is an untrusted planning-note statement. It is not acquired, not verified, and it is one of the claims the ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check must cover. Because the frozen target is the full conjecture rather than a subclass, rediscovery risk is higher, not lower: every partial route in that literature is a route this work can unknowingly repeat.

Unsourced recollection carried into this dossier and explicitly untrusted: the conjecture is reported settled for families containing a member of size one or two, for families realizable as lower semimodular lattices, for sufficiently small ground sets, and reported to have a general positive-fraction partial result below one half. None of these statements is acquired, quoted, or verified. Each must be revalidated under the ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check, and any class the slice attacks must be compared against every one of them before it is described as anything other than not_assessed.

Every frequency and family size on the trust path is an exact Python integer. The half condition is evaluated as the integer comparison 2 * freq_F(x) >= card(F), never as a division, a rational, or a floating-point ratio. Members are stored in one canonical encoding, sorted tuples of sorted ground-set labels, deduplicated before counting, and the whole canonical family is content-hashed so a claim names the exact object it was computed from. No floating-point value may appear on any trust path.

A reduction is admissible only with a proof that it preserves union closure and preserves the target property in the direction it is used. Preserving union closure alone is the standard trap: a map that sends a union-closed family to a union-closed family but can create a half-frequency element that the original lacked proves nothing about the original. Every reduction lemma must state its direction and be checked on the enumerated envelope as a falsifiability probe.

Weight-function and averaging arguments over union-closed families, and entropy or information-theoretic arguments toward a constant fraction, must not be re-derived blind. The planning dossier names rediscovery as the dominant risk for this item, so any such argument is treated as a rediscovery candidate until the ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check has run over it, and a bounded enumeration that agrees with such an argument is not evidence that the argument is new or correct.

formalization.statement: forall F a finite family of finite sets with A union B in F for all A, B in F (including A = B), and with card({A in F : A != empty}) >= 1, let U = union(A for A in F); then exists x in U with 2 * card({A in F : x in A}) >= card(F), where card(F) counts distinct members and counts the empty set when it is a member
quantifiers: forall F a finite family of finite sets that is closed under the union of any two members, including a member with itself
the hypothesis card({A in F : A != empty}) >= 1 is an explicit hypothesis, not a derived fact, and excludes exactly F = {} and F = {empty set}
exists x in U(F), the union of all members of F
forall A in F, membership of x in A is decided exactly

quantifier_mapping: forall F finite with A union B in F for all A, B in F, including A = B
with at least one nonempty member
explicit hypothesis card({A in F : A != empty}) >= 1, excluding exactly F = {} and F = {empty set}
exists x in U(F), the union of all members of F
belonging to at least half the members of F
2 * freq_F(x) >= card(F) as an integer comparison
definition_mapping: family closed under the union of any two members, empty set permitted as a member
element of the ground set U(F), the union of all members of F
number of distinct members of F, counting the empty set when it is a member

assumption_delta: No structural hypothesis is added to the target: the frozen target is the full conjecture over all finite union-closed families with a nonempty member.
The linear 3-uniform generated class appears only as the bounded first slice's waypoint; it restricts the target in no way and a theorem for it is progress rather than resolution.
The empty set is admitted as a member and counted in card(F), which strengthens the burden relative to the convention that omits it.
The nonempty-member hypothesis is explicit rather than derived, and it excludes exactly the two families F = {} and F = {empty set}.

Whether the frozen empty-set and ground-set conventions match the original statement cannot be settled before a primary source is acquired, so the strength relation is unresolved rather than equivalent.
Novelty and significance are not_assessed; no claim is made that any route or class considered here is new.
edge_case_delta: F = {} and F = {empty set} are excluded by the explicit nonempty-member hypothesis, which is the only reason the conclusion is well posed.
F = {A} with A nonempty is union-closed, has card(F) = 1, and every x in A has freq 1 >= 1/2, so it satisfies the claim.
The empty member contributes to card(F) and to no frequency, so it works against the claim and is deliberately retained.
Equality in the half condition satisfies the frozen non-strict inequality and is not a violation.
Inside the waypoint class, pairwise disjoint generators attain equality for arbitrarily large families, so no strict-inequality strengthening is available even in that special case.
A generator-based encoding never determines card(F): overlapping generators collapse distinct unions, so card(F) must be read off the deduplicated member set.

success_criteria: a rigorous proof of the frozen conjecture under the frozen conventions
an exact counterexample: a canonical content-hashed union-closed family with at least one nonempty member, exact integer frequencies, and a replayed independent check that no element reaches half
a proved theorem for an exactly stated structural class, recorded as bounded progress toward the conjecture and never as its resolution

a proved reduction that replaces the conjecture by an exactly stated smaller class of potential minimal counterexamples, with preservation of union closure and of the target property proved in the direction used
or an explicit unresolved outcome that records the smallest remaining obligation, which is the realistic outcome for a full-conjecture target and is not a failure
stopping_rules: stop on an exact certificate: a replayed counterexample family or a completed proof of the frozen conjecture
stop when fresh model spend for this target reaches USD 20
stop when no proof obligation has been discharged and no new exclusion recorded for two consecutive review points

never promote a theorem for a bounded structural class, or exhaustion of the bounded enumeration envelope, into the frozen conjecture, and never present the absence of a counterexample as evidence for it
